bug_report_content:
id: 1105
status: Fixed
summary: Constructor types that return all or unknown fail to parse
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 0
commentCount: 8
Comment 0 (2013-09-30): Constructor types that return the all type or the unknown type currently fail to parse: /** @type {function(new:?)} */ var foo = function() {}; /** @type {function(new:*)} */ var bar = function() {}; foo.js:1: ERROR - Bad type annotation. type not recognized due to syntax error /** @type {function(new:?)} */ var foo = function() {}; ^ foo.js:2: ERROR - Bad type annotation. type not recognized due to syntax error /** @type {function(new:*)} */ var bar = function() {}; ^ This is an issue for a code generator that I'm working on.
Comment 1 (2013-10-01): This seems similar to issue 790
Comment 2 (2013-10-08): The parse simply needs to change from only accepting a type name to accepting a type (a one line change + tests, I would think). It seems reasonable that this could be a record type or anything else. The work around it to use a typedef: /** @typedef {?} */ var Unknown; /** @type {function(new:Unknown)} */
Comment 3 (2013-11-02): I'm not convinced we should allow {function(new:*)}, because {function(new:string)} is impossible. The proper way to express this is {function(new:Object)}. however, we should probably emit a more sensible warning, rather than treating it as a syntax error.
Comment 4 (2013-11-02): posted a fix here: https://codereview.appspot.com/21200043/
